paragraphs.text: Stomatin-deficient cryohydrocytosis (sdCHC) is a rare form of stomatocytosis. Its red cells leak cations when cold, and patients have hemolytic anemia and hepatosplenomegaly. It is also associated with cataracts, seizures, mental retardation, and movement disorder (Flatt et al., 2011). Flatt et al. (2011) found that the disorder was associated with mutations in SLC2A1, which caused both loss of glucose transport and a cation leak.

paragraphs.text: Fricke et al. (2004) described 5 cases of stomatin-deficient hereditary stomatocytosis that differed in how the passive K+ leak depended on temperature. In 3 cases, the leak varied with temperature in a simple monotonic way. In the other 2, the leak was lowest at about 20 to 25 degrees C and the cells were extremely leaky at 0 degrees C, a phenotype known as cryohydrocytosis. The authors stated that these 2 patients were the only known cases of stomatin-deficient cryohydrocytosis. Both had a congenital syndrome of mental retardation, seizures, cataracts, and massive hepatosplenomegaly. The authors suggested that this probably defined a new haemato-neurologic syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Bawazir et al. (2012) reported an infant who presented with erratic hyperkalemia, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, anemia, hepatic dysfunction, and microcephaly. Seizures developed later, and developmental milestones were delayed. MRI and CT scans of the brain showed multiple abnormalities, including periventricular calcification. The child had visual impairment due to both cataracts and retinal dysfunction. The authors noted that this was the fourth pedigree described with the syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Lande et al. (1982) used SDS gel electrophoresis to separate erythrocyte membrane band 7 into 3 components of about 30, 28, and 26 kD. The 28-kD component was decreased in both a patient with hereditary stomatocytosis and a patient with cryohydrocytosis. On 2-dimensional electrophoresis, the 28-kD component separated into 2 proteins, 22 x 8 and 60 x 8. Protein 22 x 8 was completely absent in both patients, whereas 60 x 8 was present as usual.
